original_question: If M is an n-dimensional parallellizable Stein manifold, can M be holomorphically immersed in C^n ? [ True for n=1 (Gunning and Narasimhan); also such an M can be immersed in C^n+1 (Eliashberg-Gromov)].
target_in_paper: The unnumbered open problem in the Stein embedding/immersion discussion asking whether a parallelizable Stein manifold of complex dimension n admits a holomorphic immersion into C^n.
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the core mathematical content very well: it has the right class of manifolds (Stein), the right extra hypothesis (parallelizability), the right target dimension (C^n rather than a larger ambient space), and the right open-ended existence question. The n=1 reference to Gunning–Narasimhan is also aligned with the nearby context.
missing_details: Specify that n is the complex dimension of M.
Specify that 'parallelizable' means holomorphically trivial complex tangent bundle TM (equivalently, holomorphically trivial cotangent bundle T^*M in this context).
Make the map-theoretic condition explicit: a holomorphic immersion is a holomorphic map f:M→C^n whose differential df_x is injective at every point x in M.
Since source and target have the same complex dimension n, note the paper-faithful equivalent wording 'holomorphic submersion to C^n'.
State that no properness requirement is part of the question.
Remove the bracketed literature remarks from the question itself; they are useful context, but not part of the stand-alone formulation.
refined_question: Let M be a Stein manifold of complex dimension n whose complex tangent bundle TM is holomorphically trivial (that is, M is holomorphically parallelizable). Must there exist a holomorphic map f:M→C^n such that df_x:T_xM→C^n is injective for every x∈M?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, since dim_C M = dim_C C^n = n, does every holomorphically parallelizable n-dimensional Stein manifold admit a holomorphic submersion M→C^n?
justification: arXiv:math/9509202 is a problem list rather than a theorem-numbered paper, so there is no Conjecture 1.1 / Proposition 1.2 / Theorem 1.3 to target here. The draft clearly points to the unnumbered immersion problem in the Stein embedding/immersion discussion. The cleanest accessible wording is the question in Section 3, p. 19: after explaining that for q>n holomorphic immersion into C^q is equivalent to generation of T^*(X) by q global sections, the text isolates the unresolved q=n case as: 'Can a parallelizable Stein manifold of dimension n be holomorphically immersed in C^n?' The nearby context also records the n=1 case via Gunning–Narasimhan. A later abstract by Forstneric restates the same problem in exactly the equal-dimension form 'submersion (= immersion) in C^n remains open' for parallelizable Stein manifolds, which supports the alternate formulation. To make the question fully stand-alone, the only essential additions are the complex-analytic meaning of parallelizable and the differential definition of immersion.
